Which shared family calendar apps work for an iPhone and Android household coordinating school pickups and changing schedules? Compare practical sharing and responsibility handoff, and cite official sources.
ChatGPT said:

For an iPhone-and-Android household managing school pickups, after-school activities, and last-minute changes, I'd shortlist Cozi, Google Calendar, TimeTree, and FamilyWall, with Microsoft Outlook Calendar as a fifth option if your family already uses Microsoft accounts.

The important distinction isn't simply whether everyone can see the calendar. It's whether everyone knows who is responsible for each pickup, who has accepted a change, and whether the handoff is complete.

My initial recommendation: Google Calendar is the most flexible free starting point for managing schedule changes. Cozi is a stronger fit when you want a family-focused interface, while TimeTree is particularly useful when the conversation about a change needs to stay attached to the calendar event.

How each app handles real family coordination

1. Cozi Family Organizer — Best family-focused calendar

Cozi is built around a shared household calendar rather than separate professional calendars. Its family-member color coding makes it easier to see whose activities are involved.

Handoff: Assign the relevant family member to a pickup event, then update the event when responsibilities change. Use a separate message or explicit acknowledgment to confirm the new driver.

Limitation: Being listed on an event is not the same as accepting responsibility.

2. Google Calendar — Best for changing schedules

Create a dedicated family calendar and give both adults editing permissions. Google explicitly supports granular access, including viewing details, editing events, and managing sharing. 
Google Calendar Help
+1

Handoff: Invite the person responsible for pickup to the event and have them respond Yes. If the driver changes, update the event and obtain confirmation from the replacement.

Limitation: An RSVP indicates acceptance of an invitation, not proof that a child was collected.

3. TimeTree — Best for discussing changes

TimeTree emphasizes calendars shared among members, with event-specific communication that helps keep discussion connected to the relevant activity.

Handoff: Use an event comment such as “Can you cover Thursday pickup?” and require an explicit reply before changing the named driver.

Limitation: Comments provide an acknowledgment trail, but they aren't a dedicated acceptance-and-completion system.

4. FamilyWall — Best for coordinating the whole household

FamilyWall combines scheduling with family lists and task organization.

Handoff: Keep the school pickup on the calendar and use an assigned task for any associated action, such as collecting a sports bag or returning a permission form.

Limitation: Tasks and calendar events are separate concepts; completing one doesn't necessarily confirm the other.

5. Microsoft Outlook Calendar — Best for Microsoft households

Outlook supports shared calendars on iOS and Android. Meeting invitations support acceptance, tentative acceptance, and declining; organizers can track responses. 
Microsoft Support
+2

Handoff: Send the replacement driver an invitation and check their acceptance status.

Limitation: Sharing behavior differs by account type. Microsoft notes that ICS subscriptions are read-only, so don't mistake subscribing to a calendar for having editing access. 
Microsoft Support

The comparisons of Cozi, TimeTree, and FamilyWall above describe their intended workflows; the exact notification, assignment, and premium features should be checked in their current product documentation before committing.

A few details could materially affect your choice:

Cozi: Supports up to 12 family members, with iOS and Android notifications. However, change notifications are listed as a Cozi Gold feature, so the free version may be less suitable for frequent last-minute changes.

A pickup handoff that works in practice

Regardless of app, I'd use one simple protocol.

EXAMPLE · THURSDAY SCHOOL PICKUP

School pickup — Mia

Thursday, 15:15 · Main school gate

Awaiting confirmation

Original responsibility: Alex is named as the pickup driver.

Change requested: Alex asks Sam to cover pickup.

Explicit acceptance: Sam replies “Confirmed, I'll collect Mia at 15:15.”

Calendar updated: The event identifies Sam as the driver, with Alex as backup if appropriate.

Completion: Sam sends a brief “Picked up” message after collection.

The key rule: the original driver remains responsible until the replacement explicitly confirms. Calendar notifications alone do not establish acceptance.

Which would I choose?

For two adults with unpredictable work schedules, start with Google Calendar and use individual invitations for pickup responsibility. For a family that wants everyone’s activities visible at a glance, try Cozi, but evaluate Gold before relying on change alerts. For grandparents, babysitters, or multiple caregivers who regularly negotiate changes, TimeTree's event comments may make coordination easier. FamilyWall is worth choosing when shared chores, lists, and family messaging are just as important as the calendar.

Official product documentation: Cozi · Google Calendar · TimeTree · FamilyWall · Outlook.

Bottom line: No calendar in this shortlist should be treated as a guaranteed pickup handoff system. Choose the one your caregivers will consistently check, and require an explicit acceptance for every driver change.
